hypotheses.justification: The conclusion remains true for any `v`: `individualize` uses `p.pos[v]!` only to choose the cell whose `cst` entries it updates, and the update preserves every existing cell start under `Part.WF`. If `v < n`, `hp.posLt` shows that position is in range; otherwise `hp.posSize` makes `p.pos[v]!` the out-of-bounds default `0`. For `n = 0` the refinement goal is vacuous; for `n > 0`, position `0` is valid. The proof can establish the `individualize_cst_getElemD` formula directly from `individualize_cst_eq` and `setCstFrom_getElemD`, using `hp` at the chosen position; on the updated interval, `hp.cellCst` says the old `cst` value is the cell start, so an old start cannot lie in the interval. The `Part.WF` hypothesis is still needed: without it, an arbitrary `cst` array can have a start inside the interval that individualization overwrites.
